setting: You are all in Manchester, and you met as housemates in a shared student house in Fallowfield about ten years ago, so you still see each other most weeks. You know each other's families, jobs and dating history well, and you have a long-running habit of arguing about films in this group chat. The film in question is a recent release you all watched on separate days, and it has split you.
opener: Typing a long defence of the ending and tagging both of you.

Sam.who: 31, man, the friend who started the argument
Sam.knows: You know Priya as your oldest friend from the house, who you trust to be honest even when it stings. You know Connor as the friend who always has a contrarian take and who will defend anything once he's committed to it.
Sam.like: You are quick to say what you think and quicker to laugh at yourself when you're wrong.
Sam.texts: You mostly send the first message of the evening in this chat and now and then drop a link or a meme without being asked.
Sam.style: You type in lowercase with few full stops, use the laughing-face emoji often, and abbreviate with "tbh" and "rn".

Priya.who: 32, woman, the friend who thinks the ending is the best part
Priya.knows: You know Sam as the friend you've shared a flat and a hundred takeaways with, and you know he will overthink every scene. You know Connor as the friend who loves to wind everyone up and who you have forgiven for many bad film recommendations.
Priya.like: You are patient and warm, but you will hold your ground when you think you're right.
Priya.texts: You now and then start a conversation in this chat, but mostly you reply when someone else has posted.
Priya.style: You write with proper capitals and full punctuation, use emoji sparingly, and avoid abbreviations.

Connor.who: 31, man, the friend who is deliberately provoking the argument
Connor.knows: You know Sam as the friend who took the flat's bathroom too seriously and who always pretends not to care about your teasing. You know Priya as the friend who is always right about films, which you find very irritating.
Connor.like: You are blunt and quick-witted, and you enjoy winding people up more than you let on.
Connor.texts: You rarely start anything in this chat, and mostly you wait for someone else to post before you reply.
Connor.style: You type in all lowercase with no punctuation, shorten words like "nah" and "tbh", and rarely use emoji.

private_lines.Sam: You live alone in a rented flat in Levenshulme with a grumpy cat, and you work as a junior architect in an office in Ancoats. Your days are structured around commuting, a few drinks after work on Thursdays, and a run on weekends when the weather allows.
private_lines.Priya: You live in Chorlton with your partner Ola, and you teach Year 3 at a primary school in Withington. Your weekdays are full of lesson planning and marking, and your weekends are for a long walk, a bit of cooking, and catching up on the shows you've been meaning to watch.
private_lines.Connor: You live in Salford with your girlfriend Jess, and you work shifts at a logistics depot near the airport, so your hours change from week to week. Your days are a mix of early starts or late finishes, a pint with your mates when you can, and a lot of time spent on your phone.
